title: DSA - Insertion Sort Best & Worst Case
description:
## Best Case
If the array is already sorted, each element is already in the right place. The inner loop does zero shifts every time.

```
[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
 key=2: compare with 1, already in place. 1 comparison.
 key=3: compare with 2, already in place. 1 comparison.
 key=4: compare with 3, already in place. 1 comparison.
 key=5: compare with 4, already in place. 1 comparison.
```
Total: n-1 comparisons = **O(n)**

## Worst Case
If the array is reverse sorted, every element must shift ALL the way to the front.

```
[5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
 key=4: shift 5 right, insert 4. 1 shift.
 key=3: shift 5,4 right, insert 3. 2 shifts.
 key=2: shift 5,4,3 right, insert 2. 3 shifts.
 key=1: shift 5,4,3,2 right, insert 1. 4 shifts.
```
Total: 1+2+3+4 = 10 = **O(n²)**


---
## Question:
What is the best case time complexity of insertion sort AND what input causes it?
b3t: O(n log n) - nearly sorted array
